1932, January
FR. SOLANUS, NOTEBOOK NO. 5.
Page 16 Cont.
Jan. 14 Escapes prison Sentence - Alfred Schobett about 40 found guilty of taking $7800. by two juries and pleading guil y was expected to go to state's prison for 10 to 20 yrs is enrolled by phone - day of final trial - 5 yrs. probation.
Page 17 Jan. 15 First thunderstorm this a.m. - "Early thunder - Late Spring."
Marjorie Austin - 18 - always an invalid now T.B. Mother asks prayers - son 20 also now T.B.
Jan. 18
"Darkest Hour before Day" ?!? Mr. Vernon Mem'l Park - Park es- tates - shocked this P.M. Court decision reported against founder - Rae Garland and Partner - They decide to go to Judge Sample in Ann Arbor for redress against outrage. In meantime all are en- rolled in Mass Association ... P.S. Prosecutor demands all books and belonging as declared "receiver .. ...
Jan. 19 Order of court apointing Katzhausen Receiver - found unsigned by Judge Sample .... Hope revived Jan. 27th G's friend - B. Smicking is apointed Receiver instead - Jan. 27 Judge apoints B.S. as re- ceiver as proposed by Mr. Garland. March 17 Report To-day above case dismissed from further hearing in Court Judge Sample having so declared last Saturday March 17. Dec. 3rd Case form- ally thrown out of Ct.
Page 18 Jan. 19 Bernard - of Port Huron - 7 yrs. - unable to leave wheel chair
Mrs. Blum - Husband died of stroke and she took one also before he died. She does not know of her husband's death - now has had 2nd stroke ....
Mrs. Cunningham - breast Cancer Baby Rime - 2 - not walking Mrs. Franchel Trang
Andrew Horiski - 51 - Port Austin - ailing-big man but can hardly walk.
Krausmann - four little ones down with scarlet fever.
Mrs. Louise accident serious
